statement: The floor of a gazebo is a regular polygon with $12$ sides. What is the measure of each interior angle of the floor?

choices.misconception: I divided $360^\circ$ by $12$, but that gives each exterior angle, not the interior angle.
I used $180(n - 1)$ for the angle sum, so I got $180 \cdot 11 = 1980$ and $1980 \div 12 = 165$.
I used $360(n - 2)$ for the angle sum, so I got $360 \cdot 10 = 3600$ and $3600 \div 12 = 300$.

hints: Start with the sum of all the interior angles of a polygon.
The interior angles of an $n$-sided polygon add to $180(n - 2)$ degrees. In a regular polygon they are all equal, so divide by $n$.
The angles add to $180 \cdot 10 = 1800$ degrees, shared equally among $12$ angles.

solutions.reliable: The interior angles of a $12$-sided polygon add to $180(12 - 2) = 1800^\circ$. All $12$ angles are equal, so each one is $1800 \div 12 = 150^\circ$.
solutions.elegant: The exterior angles of any convex polygon add to $360^\circ$, so each exterior angle here is $360 \div 12 = 30^\circ$. Each interior angle is $180^\circ - 30^\circ = 150^\circ$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
